Even as renewable investments surge globally, now exceeding USD 1.8 trillion annually and outpacing fossil fuels two-to-one, overall energy investment across Eurasia has fallen by nearly 30% since 2015.
 
Yet the region holds vast untapped potential. Regional cooperation is already reshaping its energy future, such as the recent MoU between Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan to advance the Caspian Green Energy Corridor, creating a new axis for renewable power trade, jobs, and local value chains.
 
This region will be the backdrop for this year’s 14th International Forum on Energy for Sustainable Development in Skopje, North Macedonia, where I joining dialogues o how too translate such initiatives from ambition to implementation - scaled through digital, financial, and human capital:
 
1️⃣ Digital Transformation
AI forecasting, smart grids, and digital twins are redefining how power systems are planned and operated. enabling predictive maintenance, dynamic balancing of renewables, and lower system costs.
 
2️⃣ Financial Reform
Redirecting fossil-fuel subsidies, still over USD 1.5 trillion globally, toward clean energy and social protection can unlock regional capital for distributed solar, e-mobility, and efficiency retrofits.
 
3️⃣ Youth Leadership
Young innovators are designing the next generation of clean-energy solutions. Their work shows that innovation ecosystems will drive the transition.
